paper.title: Combining Diverse Information for Coordinated Action: Stochastic Bandit Algorithms for Heterogeneous Agents

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic multi-agent bandit with heterogeneous agent sensitivities
unmapped: Each of A agents has a known sensitivity s_a in (0,1]; agent a pulling arm n gets reward Bern(s_a*mu_n)
Super-arm is an injective assignment of A agents to N arms; reward is sum of agent rewards, so super-arm value is sum_a s_a*mu_{f(a)}
Learner (centralized planner) knows all agent sensitivities
settings.definition_quote: There are $A$ agents $\mathcal{A}=\{a\}_{a=1}^A$, $N$ arms ... The state of arm $n$ at time $t$ is a random variable $X_{t,n}\sim$ Bern$(\mu_n)$ ... $Y_{t,a,n}\sim \text{Bern}(s_a\mu_n)$. ... $R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{a=1}^As_a\left(\mu_{f^\star(a)}-\mu_{f_t(a)}\right)$.

conditions: sensitivities s_a in (0,1] known to the planner
each agent assigned to a distinct arm (A <= N)
tuning: confidence parameter delta in (0,1) used in the confidence width

source.label: theorem:min-width-regret
source.quote: Suppose we act according to the \textsc{Min-Width} algorithm. Then $\forall\delta\in(0,1)$, the cumulative regret at time $T$ is bounded by \mathbb{P}\left[R_T<A(N-1)+2\sqrt{2ANT\ln\left(\frac{2NG(T,A)}{\delta}\right)}\frac{\max\mathcal{S}}{\min\mathcal{S}}\right]>1-\delta.

results.notes: Paper's N (arms) mapped to K, A (agents = arms pulled per round) mapped to m. Restated as Theorem 4 in appendix. Since G(T,A)<(T+1)^A, the paper notes the time dependence is O(sqrt(T log T)). Regret is defined through means; bound holds w.p. >1-delta.
